en: The waling-waling is an epiphytic orchid that grows high on tree branches in the clouds of Mount Kitanglad.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that allow it to hunt small insects in the dark forests of Bohol.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park protects a vast coral atoll that provides a habitat for hundreds of marine fish species.
Female milkfish, locally called bangus, release thousands of eggs into the ocean where they hatch into tiny fry.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito transmits the dengue virus to humans when it bites them after feeding on infected blood.
The tamaraw is a small, horned buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro that grazes on grass and ferns.
Mangrove trees in Philippine coastal areas have specialized above-ground roots that absorb oxygen from the air during high tide.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle uses its sharp talons to hunt flying lemurs in the rainforests of Mindanao.
Enzymes in human saliva immediately begin breaking down the complex carbohydrates found in a typical Filipino meal of rice.
The tropical pitcher plant Nepenthes alata catches and digests insects using slippery, fluid-filled leaves to survive in nutrient-poor soil.
The Philippine warty frog begins its life cycle as a gill-breathing aquatic tadpole before metamorphosing into an adult.
The abaca plant, native to the Philippines, produces strong leaf fibers used to make durable Manila ropes and paper.
